question: What is the duration and title of the Medical Laboratory Technology degree program?
expected_answer: The course title is B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology, and the duration of the program is 4 years.

question: Which subjects are included in the theoretical component of the second year of the B.Sc MLT program?
expected_answer: Haematology and Blood Banking, and Histopathology and Cytopathology.

question: What are the eligibility criteria and documents required for admission to the B.Sc MLT program?
expected_answer: Documents required: Completed B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology application form, Copy of Matriculation Certificate, Copy of F.Sc / Equivalent Examination Certificate with detailed marks sheet, Copy of entry test result card, and 3 passport size photographs. General requirements: Securing pass percentage in the entry test, qualifying the interview successfully, and having up to mark credentials.

question: What is the passing percentage in each component of the professional examinations, and how many attempts are allowed for the final examination?
expected_answer: The passing score in each component is 50%, and the final examination must be cleared in a maximum of 4 attempts.

question: What is the breakdown of theory and internal assessment marks for Paper-I (Basic Anatomy & Physiology) in the First Professional Examination?
expected_answer: The paper consists of one Theory Paper of maximum 90 marks and Internal Assessment of 10 marks (5 marks each for Basic Anatomy and Basic Physiology), totaling 100 marks.

question: How many short essay questions and MCQs are included in Section I (Haematology) of Paper-I in the Second Professional Examination, and what are their respective marks?
expected_answer: Section I (Haematology) consists of 8 short essay questions carrying 5 marks each (total 40 marks for essays) and 40 MCQs carrying 1 mark each, totaling 80 marks.

question: What is the total mark allocation for the Third Professional B.Sc Medical Laboratory Technology Examination across all papers?
expected_answer: The total marks for the Third Professional Examination is 600.

question: List the recommended textbooks for Basic Anatomy as stated in the curriculum.
expected_answer: Essentials of anatomy and physiology by Seely, Stephens, and Tate (4th ed); Anatomy & Physiology by Ross & Wilson; General Anatomy by Laeeq Hussain; General Anatomy by Dr Ghulam Ahmad; Anatomy by D. R. Johnson & K. L. Moore; Color Atlas of anatomy by Mc Minn; Lasts Anatomy by R.M.H Mcminn.

question: What are the specific topics covered under Cell Injury and Adaptation in General Pathology?
expected_answer: Cell Injury covers Reversible and Irreversible Injury, Fatty change, Pigmentation, Pathologic calcification, Necrosis and Gangrene. Cellular adaptation covers Atrophy, Hypertrophy, Hyperplasia, Metaplasia, and Aplasia.

question: What are the components of the brain stem described in the syllabus?
What are the general components and devices included in a personal computer system as listed under Computer Education?
expected_answer: Hardware, Software, System Software, Application Software, Equipment/devices in Personal computer system (Input devices, Output devices, Storage devices, and The processor).

question: What are the special stains in Haematology listed in the syllabus?
expected_answer: Peroxidase stain, Sudan Black B, Periodic Acid Schiff (PAS) Stain, Feulgan reaction, Histochemical techniques for alkaline phosphatase, and Miscellaneous stains (Giemsa, Prussian blue reaction).

question: Describe the two methods of sectioning tissues detailed in the Histopathology course outlines.
expected_answer: The Paraffin method of sectioning tissue (which involves tissue dehydration, clearing, paraffin infiltration, block making, section cutting with a rotary microtome, and fixing sections to slides) and The Freezing Method of Sectioning (which involves freezing tissues and cutting sections using a freezing microtome).

question: What are the sub-topics listed under Urine analysis in Chemical Pathology on Page 61, and how do they continue onto Page 62?
expected_answer: Page 61 covers the composition of glomerular filtrate, changes occurring in tubules, normal urine physical properties and composition, pathological constituents and determination, and kidney function tests, along with quantitative analysis of urine for constituents like amino acids, Bence-Jones proteins, calcium, and urea. Page 62 continues with specific Renal Function Tests including Inulin and Creatinine clearance (GFR), Para-aminohippurate clearance, maximum rate of tubular excretion of P-amino-hippurate, maximum rate of reabsorption of glucose, and clinical assessment classifications such as BUN, serum urea, PSP test, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, serum uric acid, and electrolytes.
